name: LMZ23605TZX_NOPB
title: LMZ23605: 5 A step-down power module, 6 V to 36 V in, 0.8 V to 6 V out
summary: A complete synchronous buck converter in a 7-pin TO-PMOD package (10.16 mm × 9.85 mm) with the inductor and some input capacitance inside; two resistors and three capacitors outside make a working supply. It takes 6 V to 36 V and delivers 0.8 V to 6 V at up to 5 A (30 W at most), switching at 812 kHz or locked to a 650 kHz to 950 kHz clock. It has a precision enable for programmable UVLO, external soft-start or tracking, output overvoltage, current-limit and thermal protection, and starts into a prebiased output. Heat leaves through a large exposed pad into the board copper.
key_figures: 0.796 V typ, 0.776 to 0.816 V over TJ
812 kHz typ free-running; sync 650 to 950 kHz

notes: All variants are the same LMZ23605 module in the 7-pin NDW package, 10.16 mm × 9.85 mm nominal body; they differ only in packing: TZ in tubes of 45, TZE on reels of 250, TZX on reels of 500.
The bill of materials names the module LMZ23605TZ.

pins.name: VIN
pins.function: Supply input, 6 V to 36 V. A little capacitance is inside; external input capacitors go from this pin to the exposed pad (PGND).

pins.name: SYNC
pins.function: Clock input. A CMOS square wave from 650 kHz to 950 kHz sets the switching frequency; ground it when unused, and the module runs at 812 kHz typical.

pins.name: EN
pins.function: Enable, to a precision comparator with a 1.279 V rising threshold. Once enabled it sources 21 µA so that a divider gives hysteresis.

pins.name: AGND
pins.function: Analog ground and the reference for all voltages; must be tied to PGND (the exposed pad) outside the module.

pins.name: FB
pins.function: Feedback to the regulation amplifier and overvoltage comparators; regulates at 0.796 V. It takes the tap of the divider that runs from VOUT to AGND.

pins.name: SS/TRK
pins.function: Soft-start and tracking. A capacitor on this pin lengthens the 1.6 ms internal soft-start; a divider from a higher-priority rail makes the output track it.

pins.name: VOUT
pins.function: Output, from the internal inductor. The output capacitor connects between this pin and the exposed pad.

pins.name: PGND
pins.function: Exposed pad: power ground for the power stage and the main heat path. Not joined to AGND inside; connect it to pin 4 on the board.

circuits.title: Simplified application
circuits.description: The smallest working design: one input capacitor, one output capacitor, a soft-start capacitor and the two feedback resistors that set the output. SYNC, AGND and PGND all go to ground, so the module runs on its own oscillator; EN is brought out as a control input.

parts.note: Sized for the wanted output with the output voltage equation; 3.32 kΩ for 3.3 V.
Sized with RFBT; 1.07 kΩ for 3.3 V.

circuits.title: Typical application, 3.3 V at 5 A
circuits.description: The full reference design, 3.3 V out at up to 5 A from a 7 V to 36 V input. RENT and RENB divide the Enable input down to EN so the module turns on at about 5.46 V; the 5.1 V zener D1 keeps the divider tap inside the EN rating at high input, and RENH adds hysteresis. RFBT and RFBB set 3.3 V; RFRA sits in series with RFBT. CSS stretches the soft-start. The input has two 10 µF and two 0.047 µF ceramics plus an optional 150 µF aluminium bulk part; the output has a 220 µF polymer part, an optional 100 µF ceramic and two 0.047 µF ceramics. RSN loads the SYNC line to ground. Parts marked optional may be left off.

parts.note: optional; aluminium, 50 V, radial G; Panasonic EEE-FK1H151P
optional; 0.5 W, SOD-123; Diodes Inc. MMSZ5231BS-7-F

notes: CO2 is listed as X7R; its part number C3225X5R0J107M is an X5R part.

circuits.title: Tracking divider on SS/TRK
circuits.description: A 2.5 V module output made to follow a 3.3 V master rail at power-up. RTKT and RTKB divide the master rail onto SS/TRK in the same ratio as RFBT and RFBB divide the output onto FB; no soft-start capacitor is fitted. Only the SS/TRK and FB pins take part.

circuits.title: Enable divider with hysteresis and clamp
circuits.description: The precision-UVLO network on EN: RENT from VIN and RENB to ground set the turn-on input voltage (about 5.46 V with these values), RENH between the divider tap and EN adds falling-edge hysteresis through the 21 µA current EN sources once enabled, and the 5.1 V zener clamps the tap so EN stays within its rating at a 36 V input.
notes: Inside the module EN has a 2.0 MΩ pull-up to VIN, a 21 µA source from the 5 V internal supply switched on once enabled, and a comparator against 1.279 V.

operation.text: A synchronous buck with internal compensation and emulated peak current-mode control. The inductor current is sampled near the end of the off-time, at its valley, and that sample plus an added ramp stands in for the peak current of the next cycle. Because nothing needs to be blanked or filtered at the start of the on-time, very short on-times work, which suits large step-down ratios. The output is regulated against an internal reference of about 0.8 V.

The module holds the regulator IC, a 3.3 µH shielded inductor, a little ceramic input capacitance, the bootstrap capacitor, a linear regulator for the internal supply and a 2 MΩ pull-up from VIN to EN. No output capacitance is inside.

SYNC accepts a clock from 650 kHz to 950 kHz; the switching frequency locks to it. The input switches at about 1.4 V and should be driven to about twice that, for example from 3.3 V logic through roughly 1.5 kΩ. Unused, SYNC goes to ground directly or through 1.5 kΩ or less. A steady high level on SYNC stops switching altogether. Free-running frequency is 812 kHz typical.
If FB rises above 0.86 V the error amplifier output is driven low and the output falls.

Two limits act. The low-side limit watches the synchronous MOSFET during the off-time: above 5.4 A typical the next cycle is not started, and cycles stay blocked until the current falls; when this limit acts the switching frequency typically halves. The DC current limit depends on duty cycle. The high-side limit, 7 A typical, turns the top MOSFET off at once for the rest of that cycle, and the output falls.

At a junction temperature of 165 °C typical the module stops switching, the output falls and the soft-start capacitor is discharged. When the junction cools below about 150 °C (15 °C hysteresis) SS is released and the output ramps up again. Maximum output current at high input voltage may need extra derating at high temperature.

The module starts cleanly into an output that is already partly charged, for instance by another rail through logic. In the start-up example the output sits at 1.5 V, then once enabled rises to 3.3 V at a rate set by CSS.

With a divider from a master rail on SS/TRK in place of the soft-start capacitor, the module output follows the master during the master’s power-up, typically within 0.15 V. The divider ratio is usually the same as the feedback divider, and its resistors should be low enough that the 50 µA SS/TRK current has little effect. The module’s own soft-start must be shorter than the master’s ramp. Tracking applies only while the master powers up: once SS/TRK passes 0.8 V the input stops acting and the 50 µA source turns off.

At light load the module runs in discontinuous conduction, the inductor current falling to zero in each cycle while its average equals the load; output ripple is usually higher in this mode. Above the critical load it runs in continuous conduction, the inductor current never reaching zero. The boundary follows the DCM/CCM boundary equation.

EN is a precision comparator input with a 1.279 V rising threshold. Left open, the internal 2 MΩ pull-up enables the module, and the internal UVLO then starts it at about 4.3 V rising input. EN can be driven from logic, or from a divider off VIN or an earlier rail to set the input voltage below which the module stays off. Once enabled, EN sources 21 µA, which gives hysteresis through the divider and an optional series RENH. In the typical application, 42.2 kΩ over 12.7 kΩ gives a 5.46 V turn-on; at 36 V that divider would put 8.33 V on EN, above its 5.5 V rating, so a 5.1 V zener clamps the tap. The clamp is not needed where the input cannot push EN past its limit.

After all UVLO conditions are met an internal ramp of 1.6 ms brings SS/TRK up; with no CSS fitted the turn-on takes about 2 ms. A capacitor on SS/TRK, charged at 50 µA, lengthens the ramp; 0.47 µF is a good first value. When SS passes 0.796 V the output is in regulation and the 50 µA source switches off. SS is discharged to ground when EN goes low, on thermal shutdown, and on internal VCC UVLO (input below about 4.3 V).

All output capacitance is external, and at least 200 µF is needed for loop stability with the internal compensation. For the lowest ripple choose low-ESR parts: tantalum, polymer or organic semiconductor; several in parallel close to the module are fine. The bank must carry at least half the peak-to-peak inductor ripple current. More capacitance lowers ripple if ESR allows. A suggested combination is 220 µF, 7 mΩ polymer plus 100 µF, 6.3 V X5R ceramic, with small ceramics added for high-frequency EMI.

The internal input capacitance is small, so external input capacitors, placed very close to the module, must take the ripple current; size them by ripple current more than by capacitance. At least 22 µF of X7R or X5R ceramic is recommended, rated at least 25% above the highest input voltage, with voltage and temperature derating allowed for. Extra bulk capacitance with some ESR can damp resonance with supply-lead inductance; the reference design carries 150 µF, 50 V aluminium for this, often not needed.

The input supply should be well regulated over 6 V to 36 V, able to deliver the peak input current, and of low enough impedance that a load transient does not dip VIN into UVLO. A supply sitting several inches or more away calls for bulk capacitance besides the ceramics; 47 µF or 100 µF electrolytic is typical.

Keep the two switched current loops small: put CIN1 right at VIN and the PGND exposed pad, and ground the input and output capacitors to a local top-side plane joined to the pad. Return the FB, SS/TRK and EN components to AGND (pin 4) and tie AGND to PGND at one point. Keep RFBT and RFBB close to FB with little copper on that node, and route them away from the module body. Make input and output copper wide, and sense the output at the load with its own feedback trace. Under the exposed pad use a 6 × 10 array of thermal vias, 8 mil minimum via diameter at 39 mil (1.0 mm) pitch, to the bottom ground plane and inner planes, with enough copper to hold the junction below 125 °C.

Estimate the loss from the highest input voltage and the mean load current, using the dissipation curves; keep the junction below 125 °C. Above about 5 W of loss, airflow or a heat sink may be needed. The copper under the pad must be tied to it; the example uses about sixty 8 mil vias at 39 mil (1.0 mm) pitch between top and bottom copper.

Pads may be solder-mask defined or not. Stencil the exposed pad at about 80% of its land area and the signal pads at 1:1. Use SAC alloy paste such as SAC 305, type 3 or finer, and a 0.125 mm to 0.15 mm stencil. Reflow per the paste supplier and SNAA214; peak reflow is 245 °C, and only one reflow is allowed. MSL is level 3 at 245 °C, 168 h.
